title: Veterans Pension Net Worth — Annual Income After the Medical Deduction
content:
# Medical deduction from annual income — Veterans Pension net worth

**Deduction.** The medical deduction for net worth is the medical figure, which is the insurance premiums counted plus the care cost, less the medical threshold, when medical expense reports are on file on the award, and nothing otherwise. The medical threshold is 5 percent of the rate category's basic rate for the medical deduction, rounded to the cent — 872.00 where that basic rate is 17440, 1141.90 where it is 22838.

**Annual income after the medical deduction** follows the deduction:

1. When the deduction is positive and smaller than the annual income, the income less the deduction is used.
2. When the deduction is positive and at least the income, no income is used.
3. Otherwise the income is used whole.

## Truth table

| Medical expense reports on file | Deduction positive | Deduction smaller than income | Annual income used |
|---|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes | income less the deduction |
| yes | yes | no | 0 |
| yes | no | — | income whole |
| no | — | — | income whole |

## Worked case (hypothetical one-dependent category; annual income 16000.00)

Premiums counted 4869.60 plus care cost 18000.00 is a medical figure of 22869.60; less 1141.90 the deduction is 21727.70, at least the income, so no income is used. With a care cost of 6000.00 instead, the medical figure is 10869.60, the deduction 9727.70 and the income used 6272.30.
